title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 3. The Account of the Twelve Forests
html:
The Lord asks the brahmana Krishnadasa to show Him Mathura-mandala, and he describes the Yamuna and the twelve forests of Vraja — seven on the western bank and five on the eastern

Verse 1

एवं तां रजनीं नीत्वा क्षणप्रायं शचीसुतः।
उत्कण्ठितः प्रदोषे च विप्रमाहूय सत्वरम्॥१॥

evaṁ tāṁ rajanīṁ nītvā kṣaṇaprāyaṁ śacīsutaḥ|
utkaṇṭhitaḥ pradoṣe ca vipramāhūya satvaram||1||

evam — thus; tam — that; rajanim — night; nitva — passing; kshana-prayam — as if a moment; shachi-sutah — the son of Shachi; utkanthitah — eager; pradoshe — at the end of the night; cha — and; vipram — the brahmana; ahuya — calling; satvaram — quickly.

1Thus, having passed that night as if it were a single moment, the son of Shachi, full of eagerness, quickly called the brahmana as the night drew to its end,

Verse 2

प्रोवाच मे दर्शय त्वं मथुरामण्डलं सखे।
येन हि परमा प्रीतिर्भवेदेवं तथा वचः॥२॥

provāca me darśaya tvaṁ mathurāmaṇḍalaṁ sakhe|
yena hi paramā prītirbhavedevaṁ tathā vacaḥ||2||

provacha — said; me — to Me; darshaya — show; tvam — you; mathura-mandalam — Mathura-mandala; sakhe — O friend; yena — by which; hi — indeed; parama — the highest; pritih — joy; bhavet — may arise; evam — so; tatha — such; vachah — words.

2and said, "Show Me Mathura-mandala, My friend! Tell Me of it in such a way that I may feel the highest joy."

Verse 3

सोऽप्याह माथुरे ब्रह्मन् यमुना सर्वतोऽधिका।
यस्यां प्रीतिं समासाद्य कृष्णः सर्वेश्वरेश्वरः॥३॥

so'pyāha māthure brahman yamunā sarvato'dhikā|
yasyāṁ prītiṁ samāsādya kṛṣṇaḥ sarveśvareśvaraḥ||3||

sah — he; api — in turn; aha — said; mathure — in the land of Mathura; brahman — O brahmana; yamuna — the Yamuna; sarvatah — above all; adhika — highest; yasyam — in whom; pritim — delight; samasadya — finding; krishnah — Krishna; sarva-ishvara-ishvarah — the Lord of all lords.

3And he replied, "O brahmana1, in the land of Mathura the Yamuna stands above all: finding delight in her,

Verse 4

गोपगोपीरसामोदी परमात्मा नराकृतिः।
खेलति स्म सुखं रासजलकेलिकुतूहली॥४॥

gopagopīrasāmodī paramātmā narākṛtiḥ|
khelati sma sukhaṁ rāsajalakelikutūhalī||4||

gopa-gopi-rasa-amodi — delighting in the rasa of the cowherd boys and the gopis; parama-atma — the Supreme Soul; nara-akritih — whose form is like that of a man; khelati sma — played; sukham — happily; rasa-jala-keli-kutuhali — fond of the rasa dance and water-play.

4Krishna — the Lord of all lords, the Supreme Soul, whose form is like that of a man, who delights in the rasa of the cowherd boys and the gopis — played happily, fond of the rasa dance and of sport in the water.

Verse 5

कालिन्द्याः पश्चिमे भागे मधुवृन्दावनं परम्।
कुमुदं खदिरं चैव तालकाम्यबहूलकम्॥५॥

kālindyāḥ paścime bhāge madhuvṛndāvanaṁ param|
kumudaṁ khadiraṁ caiva tālakāmyabahūlakam||5||

kalindyah — of the Kalindi; pashchime bhage — on the western side; madhu-vrindavanam — Madhuvana and Vrindavana; param — excellent; kumudam — Kumuda; khadiram — Khadira; cha eva — and also; tala-kamya-bahulakam — Tala, Kamya and Bahula.

5On the western side of the Kalindi lie the glorious Madhuvana and Vrindavana, and also Kumuda, Khadira, Tala, Kamya and Bahula.

Verse 6

अस्याः पूर्वे भद्रबिल्वलोहभाण्डीरनामकम्।
महद्वनं च रसिकैर्ध्यायन्ते प्रीतिहेतवे॥६॥

asyāḥ pūrve bhadrabilvalohabhāṇḍīranāmakam|
mahadvanaṁ ca rasikairdhyāyante prītihetave||6||

asyah — from her; purve — to the east; bhadra-bilva-loha-bhandira-namakam — (the forests) named Bhadra, Bilva, Loha and Bhandira; mahat-vanam — the Great Forest; cha — and; rasikaih — by the rasikas; dhyayante — are meditated upon; priti-hetave — for the sake of love.

6To the east of her lie the forests named Bhadra, Bilva, Loha and Bhandira, and the Great Forest; on these the rasikas meditate for the sake of love.

Verse 7

भद्रश्रीलोहभाण्डीरमहातालखदिरकम्।
बहुलं कुमुदं काम्यं मधु वृन्दावनं तथा॥७॥

bhadraśrīlohabhāṇḍīramahātālakhadirakam|
bahulaṁ kumudaṁ kāmyaṁ madhu vṛndāvanaṁ tathā||7||

bhadra-shri-loha-bhandira-maha-tala-khadirakam — Bhadra, Shri, Loha, Bhandira, Maha(vana), Tala and Khadira; bahulam — Bahula; kumudam — Kumuda; kamyam — Kamya; madhu — Madhu; vrindavanam — Vrindavana; tatha — likewise.

7Bhadra, Shri2, Loha, Bhandira, Mahavana, Tala, Khadira, Bahula, Kumuda, Kamya, Madhu and Vrindavana —

Verse 8

द्वादशैतद्वनं रम्यं श्रीकृष्णप्रीतिदं सदा।
महत्त्वमेषां जानन्ति भक्ता नान्ये कदाचन॥८॥

dvādaśaitadvanaṁ ramyaṁ śrīkṛṣṇaprītidaṁ sadā|
mahattvameṣāṁ jānanti bhaktā nānye kadācana||8||

dvadasha — twelve; etat — these; vanam — forests; ramyam — lovely; shri-krishna-priti-dam — bestowing love for Sri Krishna; sada — always; mahattvam — the greatness; esham — of them; jananti — know; bhaktah — devotees; na — not; anye — others; kadachana — ever.

8these twelve lovely forests ever bestow love for Sri Krishna. Their greatness is known to the devotees, and never to others.

Verse 9

यमुनापश्चिमे भागे कंसस्य सदनं परम्।
अस्योत्तरे महारम्यं वृन्दारण्यं सुदुर्लभम्॥९॥

yamunāpaścime bhāge kaṁsasya sadanaṁ param|
asyottare mahāramyaṁ vṛndāraṇyaṁ sudurlabham||9||

yamuna-pashchime bhage — on the western side of the Yamuna; kamsasya — of Kamsa; sadanam — palace; param — great; asya — of it; uttare — to the north; maha-ramyam — most lovely; vrinda-aranyam — the forest of Vrinda; sudurlabham — hard to attain.

9On the western side of the Yamuna stands the great palace of Kamsa3; to the north of it lies the most lovely forest of Vrinda, so hard to attain.

Verse 10

कुमुदाख्यवनं तस्या नैरृते सुखदं हरेः।
तद्दक्षिणे खदिराख्यं वनं कृष्णसुखप्रदम्॥१०॥

kumudākhyavanaṁ tasyā nairṛte sukhadaṁ hareḥ|
taddakṣiṇe khadirākhyaṁ vanaṁ kṛṣṇasukhapradam||10||

kumuda-akhya-vanam — the forest named Kumuda; tasyah — from her (Mathura); nairrite — in the south-west; sukha-dam — giving joy; hareh — to Hari; tat-dakshine — to its south; khadira-akhyam — named Khadira; vanam — a forest; krishna-sukha-pradam — giving joy to Krishna.

10To the south-west of the city4 lies the forest named Kumuda, which gives joy to Hari; to the south of it is the forest named Khadira, which delights Krishna.

Verse 11

मथुरापश्चिमे तालवनं केशववल्लभम्।
नदी तत्र मानसाख्या गङ्गा भुवनपावनी॥११॥

mathurāpaścime tālavanaṁ keśavavallabham|
nadī tatra mānasākhyā gaṅgā bhuvanapāvanī||11||

mathura-pashchime — west of Mathura; tala-vanam — Talavana; keshava-vallabham — dear to Keshava; nadi — a river; tatra — there; manasa-akhya — named Manasa; ganga — Ganga; bhuvana-pavani — purifier of the worlds.

11To the west of Mathura is Talavana, dear to Keshava. There flows a river named Manasa-Ganga, the purifier of the worlds —

Verse 12

वृन्दारण्यपश्चिमे च गोवर्धनगिरेस्तटे।
श्रीकृष्णः क्रीडति यत्र नौकाखण्डादिलीलया॥१२॥

vṛndāraṇyapaścime ca govardhanagirestaṭe|
śrīkṛṣṇaḥ krīḍati yatra naukākhaṇḍādilīlayā||12||

vrinda-aranya-pashchime — west of the forest of Vrinda; cha — and; govardhana-gireh — of Govardhana Hill; tate — at the slope; shri-krishnah — Sri Krishna; kridati — plays; yatra — where; nauka-khanda-adi-lilaya — with the boat pastime and other sports.

12west of the forest of Vrinda, at the slope of Govardhana Hill, where Sri Krishna plays at boating and other sports5.

Verse 13

मथुरापश्चिमे गोवर्धनो नाम महागिरिः।
तस्यापि पश्चिमे काम्यवनं कृष्णरसायनम्॥१३॥

mathurāpaścime govardhano nāma mahāgiriḥ|
tasyāpi paścime kāmyavanaṁ kṛṣṇarasāyanam||13||

mathura-pashchime — west of Mathura; govardhanah — Govardhana; nama — by name; maha-girih — a great hill; tasya — of it; api — further; pashchime — to the west; kamya-vanam — Kamyavana; krishna-rasayanam — an elixir for Krishna.

13To the west of Mathura is the great hill named Govardhana, and further west still is Kamyavana, an elixir for Krishna.

Verse 14

तत्सान्निध्ये महापुण्या सरस्वती नदी शुभा।
मधुपुर्या उत्तरे च यमुनामनुधावति॥१४॥

tatsānnidhye mahāpuṇyā sarasvatī nadī śubhā|
madhupuryā uttare ca yamunāmanudhāvati||14||

tat-sannidhye — near it; maha-punya — most holy; sarasvati — the Sarasvati; nadi — river; shubha — auspicious; madhupuryah — of Madhupuri; uttare — to the north; cha — and; yamunam — the Yamuna; anudhavati — runs after.

14Near it flows the most holy and auspicious river Sarasvati, and north of Madhupuri she runs after the Yamuna.

Verse 15

ऐशान्यां मथुरायाश्च बहुलाख्यवनं शुभम्।
मनोगङ्गा समुत्तीर्य यत्र क्रीडति कंसहा॥१५॥

aiśānyāṁ mathurāyāśca bahulākhyavanaṁ śubham|
manogaṅgā samuttīrya yatra krīḍati kaṁsahā||15||

aishanyam — in the north-east; mathurayah — of Mathura; cha — and; bahula-akhya-vanam — the forest named Bahula; shubham — auspicious; mano-ganga — the Mano-Ganga; samuttirya — crossing; yatra — where; kridati — plays; kamsa-ha — the Slayer of Kamsa.

15To the north-east of Mathura is the auspicious forest named Bahula, where the Slayer of Kamsa plays after crossing the Mano-Ganga,

Verse 16

मोहनाख्यवनं चैव कथितानि महाभुज।
वनानि सप्त यमुनापश्चिमे ह परं शृणु॥१६॥

mohanākhyavanaṁ caiva kathitāni mahābhuja|
vanāni sapta yamunāpaścime ha paraṁ śṛṇu||16||

mohana-akhya-vanam — the forest named Mohana; cha eva — and also; kathitani — have been described; maha-bhuja — O mighty-armed one; vanani — forests; sapta — seven; yamuna-pashchime — west of the Yamuna; ha — indeed; param — further; shrinu — hear.

16and also the forest named Mohana6. So I have described, O mighty-armed one, the seven forests west of the Yamuna; now hear further.

Verse 17

तस्याः पूर्वकूले पञ्चवनानि रसिकेश्वर।
तत्कृपापारवश्येन लक्ष्यते विपुलं मया॥१७॥

tasyāḥ pūrvakūle pañcavanāni rasikeśvara|
tatkṛpāpāravaśyena lakṣyate vipulaṁ mayā||17||

tasyah — her; purva-kule — on the eastern bank; pancha-vanani — five forests; rasika-ishvara — O lord of rasikas; tat-kripa-paravashyena — by the power of her mercy; lakshyate — is seen; vipulam — in full; maya — by me.

17On her eastern bank, O lord of rasikas, are five forests; by the power of her mercy they have been revealed to me in full.

Verse 18

यमुनायाः सुनिकटे महारण्यं सुदुर्लभम्।
बिल्वं तत्पश्चिमे रम्यं कृष्णप्रेमफलप्रदम्॥१८॥

yamunāyāḥ sunikaṭe mahāraṇyaṁ sudurlabham|
bilvaṁ tatpaścime ramyaṁ kṛṣṇapremaphalapradam||18||

yamunayah — of the Yamuna; sunikate — very near; maha-aranyam — the Great Forest; sudurlabham — hard to attain; bilvam — Bilva; tat-pashchime — to its west; ramyam — lovely; krishna-prema-phala-pradam — bestowing the fruit of love for Krishna.

18Very near the Yamuna lies the Great Forest, hard to attain; to the west of it is lovely Bilva, which bestows the fruit of love for Krishna.

Verse 19

तस्योत्तरे लोहनामवनं भद्रवनं तथा।
भाण्डीरकवनं रम्यं कृष्णभक्तिप्रदं महत्॥१९॥

tasyottare lohanāmavanaṁ bhadravanaṁ tathā|
bhāṇḍīrakavanaṁ ramyaṁ kṛṣṇabhaktipradaṁ mahat||19||

tasya — of it; uttare — to the north; loha-nama-vanam — the forest named Loha; bhadra-vanam — Bhadravana; tatha — likewise; bhandiraka-vanam — Bhandiravana; ramyam — lovely; krishna-bhakti-pradam — bestowing devotion to Krishna; mahat — great.

19To the north of it lie the forest named Loha, and Bhadravana as well, and the great and lovely Bhandiravana, which bestows devotion to Krishna.

Verse 20

द्वादशैतद्वनं रम्यं मथुरामण्डलं प्रभो।
एतेषु विहरत्येव कृष्णो योगेश्वरेश्वरः॥२०॥

dvādaśaitadvanaṁ ramyaṁ mathurāmaṇḍalaṁ prabho|
eteṣu viharatyeva kṛṣṇo yogeśvareśvaraḥ||20||

dvadasha — twelve; etat — these; vanam — forests; ramyam — lovely; mathura-mandalam — Mathura-mandala; prabho — O Lord; eteshu — in them; viharati — sports; eva — indeed; krishnah — Krishna; yoga-ishvara-ishvarah — the Lord of the lords of yoga.

20These twelve lovely forests are Mathura-mandala, O Lord. In them Krishna, the Lord of the lords of yoga, takes His pleasure.

Verse 21

प्रत्येकं दर्शयिष्यामि यस्मात्तेऽनुग्रहो मयि।
भवेदेव हृषीकेश येन स्याद्भवमोचनम्॥२१॥

pratyekaṁ darśayiṣyāmi yasmātte'nugraho mayi|
bhavedeva hṛṣīkeśa yena syādbhavamocanam||21||

pratyekam — each one; darshayishyami — I shall show; yasmat — since; te — Your; anugrahah — favour; mayi — toward me; bhavet — will be; eva — surely; hrishikesha — O Hrishikesha; yena — by which; syat — there will be; bhava-mochanam — release from worldly existence.

21I shall show You each one of them, for Your favour, O Hrishikesha, will surely rest upon me — and through it comes release from the round of births."

Thus ends the third sarga, "The Account of the Twelve Forests" (Dvadasha-vana-prasanga), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. The brahmana Krishnadasa addresses the Lord, who is a brahmana by birth.
  2. Shri (Shrivana): another name of Bilva.
  3. Kamsa: the king of Mathura, Krishna's uncle, slain by Him.
  4. Literally "from her," apparently from Mathura.
  5. Literally "with the nauka-khanda play," apparently Krishna's boat pastime with the gopis; the exact sense of the word is unclear.
  6. The forest Mohana is not named in the lists of verses 5 and 7; it is apparently Madhuvana, which is otherwise not mentioned among the seven western forests.
